small_guidance:
- Add larger tile configs (BLOCK_OC=128, BLOCK_HW=64/128 with num_warps=8) and try num_stages=3-4; current shape is OC=64, H_OUT*W_OUT=15876, so a single BLOCK_OC=64 covering all output channels in one program eliminates the OC tiling loop and lets BLOCK_HW grow.
- Swap the loop order so KH/KW are the outer static loops and IC is innermost — this lets the same `oh+kh, ow+kw` index be reused across IC, and IC=8 is small enough that the inner loop unrolls cleanly; also load `w_vals` as a [BLOCK_OC, IC] tile via tl.dot to use tensor cores.
- Pass the spatial offsets as 2D (oh[None,:], ow[None,:]) precomputed once and use `tl.multiple_of`/`tl.max_contiguous` hints on `offs_hw` so contiguous W-dimension loads coalesce.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an explicit im2col-style GEMM using `tl.dot`: tile (BLOCK_M=BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_N=BLOCK_HW, BLOCK_K) over the reduction dim K=IC*KH*KW=72; one `tl.dot` per K-tile gives tensor-core throughput instead of the current scalar FMA outer-product accumulation, which is the main reason fast_p≈0.48.
- Use NHWC (channels-last) layout for input and output so the K dimension (IC) is contiguous in memory; permute the weight to (OC, KH, KW, IC) once in __init__ and store with channels-last strides, then loads along K coalesce naturally.
- Fuse bias + hardswish*relu in the epilogue on the accumulator (already done) and consider a persistent-CTA scheme over (N, OC_tile) iterating the spatial tile loop internally to amortize weight loads — weights are only 64*8*9=4608 floats and can be kept resident across the spatial sweep.
